description: A deputy general counsel for employment must authorize the company's response and proposed resolution of an employee discrimination and retaliation charge, while setting the investigation, agency-response, and non-monetary resolution terms.

shared_context.S1: A former employee has filed an administrative charge alleging discrimination, retaliation, and failure to accommodate a religious practice.
shared_context.S2: The agency has acknowledged receipt of the charge and requested the company's position statement.
shared_context.S3: The employee's separation was approved under the company's ordinary performance-management process, and the company has not yet made a settlement proposal.
shared_context.S4: Elena Marquez must authorize the response and any proposed resolution before they are sent; before finalizing that authorization, she follows the firm's routine of asking employment, HR, investigations, and conflicts personnel for relevant information and recording a binding decision on each proposed response and resolution term.
shared_context.S5: The charge file contains allegations concerning the supervisor's conduct, the employee's accommodation request, and the separation decision.

PF1.text: While indexing a charge exhibit uploaded yesterday, Thomas found the employee's signed accommodation request and the company's four written responses. The position statement must address the accommodation issue separately from retaliation and attach exactly those four responses; he has not yet updated the response outline.

PF2.text: In a recent exit call, the employee told Nadia that reinstatement to the former team and a neutral employment reference matter more to them than money, and that the employee would accept no monetary payment if both terms were provided. Nadia recorded the request in her HR notes but has not sent the notes to legal.

PF3.text: Maya's review of the last two years of discipline records found two similarly situated employees who received materially different discipline for comparable attendance conduct. She recommends an independent comparator review covering exactly three employees before the company asserts that discipline was consistent; her audit worksheet is still in the HR investigations folder.

PF4.text: Samuel confirmed that the proposed outside investigator previously represented the accused supervisor in a personal employment matter. That investigator must not be used; the company must appoint an independent external investigator and impose a written ethical screen before interviews begin. Samuel's conflicts check was completed this morning but is not yet on the matter checklist.

decisions.investigator_assignment: string; use exactly 'independent_external' when an independent external investigator is selected

acceptance_conditions: The agency response must address the accommodation issue separately from retaliation.
Exactly four written accommodation responses must be attached to the position statement.
The proposed resolution must authorize reinstatement to the former team, require a neutral reference, and provide no monetary payment.
An independent comparator review must cover exactly three employees before the company asserts consistent discipline.
The conflicted proposed investigator must be replaced with an independent external investigator.
A written ethical screen must be required before interviews begin.
The employee's accommodation documentation must be cited by the decision-maker as justification.
A comparator-review commitment must be recorded.

content_checks.C3: decisions['reinstatement_offered'] == True and decisions['neutral_reference_required'] == True and decisions['monetary_payment'] == 0

decisive_facts.why: The ordinary record does not identify the separate accommodation issue or the attachment set; PF1 changes the response to separate that issue and attach exactly four written responses.
Without PF2, the company has no concrete basis to authorize reinstatement to the former team, require a neutral reference, and set monetary payment at exactly zero.
The shared record contains no comparator result; PF3 changes the plan to an independent review covering exactly three employees and requires that review to be logged.

The proposed investigator appears available on the ordinary record, while PF4 changes the assignment to the exact independent_external selection and requires a written ethical screen before interviews.
